classification.difficultyReason: Find the horizontal difference between the parallel sides, then use Pythagoras to calculate the perpendicular height.

content.prompt: Find the height of the trapezium shown below.

spec.description: Unshaded trapezium with horizontal upper and lower bases, a vertical right side, a sloping left side and a red dashed perpendicular from the upper-left vertex to the lower base. Right-angle squares appear at the perpendicular foot and lower-right corner. Ordinary source blue strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Upper base 11 m, lower base 16 m and left sloping side 13 m. The required height is the dashed perpendicular. No calculated length is printed.
spec.answerVisibility: All given measurements and the construction are permanent; the height is withheld.

answer.worked:
The horizontal side of the left-hand right-angled triangle is $16-11=5\,\mathrm{m}$. Let the height be $h$ metres. By Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}h^2+5^2&=13^2\\h^2+25&=169\\h^2&=169-25\\h^2&=144\\h&=\sqrt{144}\\h&=12.\end{align*}$$
The height is $12\,\mathrm{m}$.
